$comment: Problem-report text the value-free gate must refuse, and the near misses it must let through. A `rejected` case names the `rule` whose id must appear among the rules refusing it - more than one rule may fire, and that is not a failure: a leak has a shape, not an id. An `accepted` case must be refused by NO rule, and that half is the half that keeps the gate usable: a gate that refuses a doctor finding id, an install coordinate or a hyphenated sentence is a gate an agent learns to work around. Three rows document a decided LIMIT rather than a capability (`entropy-hex-run-32`, `accepted-unqualified-rendered-call`, `accepted-hyphenated-prose`); each says so in its description, so flipping one is a decision and not a fix. The gate is deliberately STRICTER than the renderer's own redaction - `value-shape-checksum-failing-lookalike` is the row that pins it - because here a false positive is a refusal that names its rule and a false negative is a public issue. See README.md.

cases.description: the rendered narrative's own call line: a parameter shown with the value it was bound to
the call line exactly as MarkdownRenderer writes it: the qualified name is bold, so the closing ** sits between the name and the parenthesis, and each value is in backticks
the same line as it appears nested in a rendered markdown trace, which is how it reaches a clipboard
the indented-text call line, which ends with the span id: the id does not launder the value bound beside it
a returned value after the outcome arrow, where the structural form writes the bare word value
the same arrow carrying a number, because a number is a value too
a collection summary after the arrow: still the shape of what was returned, measured at runtime
an elapsed time, which only a value-carrying artifact measures
the same measurement at a coarser unit and a decimal point
the micro sign unit, which a fast call renders and a naive pattern misses
the redaction marker: it exists only where a value was blanked, so its presence proves a rendered artifact
the marker with nothing else, which is what survives a careless copy of one field
a header whose name says it carries a credential, with the credential beside it
the English baseline, assigned with an equals sign the way a properties file writes it
the Spanish for password with the tilde a Spanish team types
the same word as n + U+0303, which is what a Mac filesystem hands back
the Chinese for password, which a deny-list restated as ASCII would lose

the same binding with the key in quotes, which is what the doctor report - the one attachment every report carries - is written in. The closing quote sits between the key and the colon, so a scan anchored on adjacency alone cannot read JSON at all.
an environment assignment pasted from a shell, where the key is upper snake case
the same binding inside a pasted configuration file, which is the most likely accidental attachment
a GitHub personal access token, the credential most likely to be in the terminal a report is written from
the fine-grained spelling of the same credential, which the older prefix does not match
an AWS access key id, recognised by its prefix and its fixed length
a key with the sk- prefix, the shape a developer's own shell configuration is full of
a Slack token, whose prefix family is four letters wide
the header line of a private key block, which is enough on its own to prove a key was pasted
a JWT, anchored on the base64url encoding of a JSON object's opening brace
a payment card number at its own digit length
a Chilean RUT with the thousands dots it is printed with
the same id whose verifier is ten, which Chile writes K
a Brazilian CPF as eleven bare digits, with no separator to give it away
a Brazilian CNPJ as it is printed, slash and all
a Spanish NIE, whose leading letter is part of the shape
a French NIR in the spaced form the card is printed in
a Chinese resident identity card, eighteen characters ending in a check that may be X
a CPF whose check digits are wrong: the renderer leaves it VISIBLE and this gate still refuses it, which is the asymmetry on purpose
an opaque session token: no prefix, no shape, nothing but density to give it away
the base64url alphabet, whose underscore keeps the run intact

a 32-digit hex run. Sixteen symbols cap Shannon entropy at 4.0 bits per character and a measured sample of random hex never passed 3.97, so the hex half of this rule is carried by LENGTH, not by entropy. Deleting the length clause reopens the hole.
a 64-digit hex run: a hash, an HMAC or an opaque id, and the length clause's reason for existing
an address in the middle of a sentence, which is how a report names who hit the problem
cases.value: ada@example.com saw it first on the staging build

cases.description: the same address with a plus tag, which a naive local-part pattern drops
a macOS home directory, which carries the account name
the Linux spelling of the same thing
the Windows spelling, with backslashes and a drive letter
a terminal colour escape, which is what survives a copy out of a coloured build log
a NUL byte: never content, and the oldest way to truncate whatever reads the report next
a lone carriage return from a Windows log paste. Refused on purpose: a report is text a person wrote, and the two whitespace characters it needs are the line feed and the tab.
a right-to-left override, which reorders what a reviewer of the issue sees without changing what is stored
the structural trace's own call line: parameter NAMES and no values, which is the artifact a report is supposed to carry
the structural call line with the qualified name emphasised the way the Markdown renderer does: crossing the emphasis must not turn a names-only line into a refusal
the structural outcome marker, which is the literal word value and not a value
a thrown outcome: the exception TYPE is structure, and the message that would be a value is never there
the incomplete marker a best-effort run leaves behind
the concurrency marker, whose bracketed count is a structural fan-out and not an elapsed time
the header line, whose key is followed by a humanised test name
cases.value: scenario: Weekend trip settles with three transfers

cases.description: the structural call line as the .nt writes it since span ids: a position path opens the line, and a position is not a value
a fire-and-forget launch, whose span id opens its marker line
the sentence a verify or debug report is written in: a claim about the trace pointing at the spans it read, by id
cases.value: The trace showed #2.1 NotificationService.send firing before #2.4 PaymentGateway.confirm returned.

cases.description: an approval diff context line whose id an inserted call shifted, citing both sides
the install coordinate every report carries, which is three colon-separated fields of its own
a third-party coordinate a report quotes while describing the trap it hit
a doctor check id, which is what the step field names
the absolute doc URL every finding carries, whose slashes and hyphens must not read as an encoded run
the path the doctor's JSON report lands at, which a report names in almost every sentence

a structural artifact's full path. It is a 64-character run of the encoded-run alphabet at 3.96 bits per character, four hundredths under the ceiling: the closest legitimate string in the product to being refused as a secret.
the form the draft rewrites a home directory to, which must not then be refused as one
a deny-listed word in a sentence rather than as the key being assigned: the key here is header, and this is the report we want
cases.value: the authorization header: it never arrived at all

cases.description: a sensitive parameter NAME in a structural call line. The name is shape and may stay; only a value beside it may not.
a Java annotation, whose at-sign must not read as an email address
cases.value: the @NotTraced import was never applied to the field

cases.description: an ISO date, which is eight digits and two hyphens and is not a national id
cases.value: on 2026-09-02 the doctor reported two findings

cases.description: nine bare digits: an invoice or order number, which the renderer also leaves visible
cases.value: invoice 987654321 was the one that failed

cases.description: a hyphenated phrase past the encoded-run length. It measures 4.33 bits per character, so admitting the hyphen to the run alphabet would refuse it; the alphabet excludes the hyphen for exactly this row.
a hex-shaped word below the length floor, which is how the floor is proved to be a floor
cases.value: deadbeefcafe showed up in the stack trace

cases.description: an em dash followed by a number that is not a duration, because the unit is a word
cases.value: twelve checks — 2 findings, both in the trap family

cases.description: the two whitespace characters a report legitimately contains

a hand-typed call fragment with no qualifying type. The rendered artifact ALWAYS writes Type.method(...), which is what the rendered-call rule is anchored on, so this shape is reached only by its key's name. Known limit, kept visible: widening the rule would flip this row to rejected.
